title: Choose a proportionate development procedure
summary: Select useful clarification, planning, implementation and review procedures without importing an entire tool library as policy.

sections.label: Use this workflow
sections.text: Use when adopting agent guidance for a feature or repair. Keep the request, existing repository conventions and acceptance criteria authoritative.

sections.label: Inputs
items: Agreed outcome, repository revision, constraints and relevant existing instructions.
One proposed procedure and its source revision.
Expected deliverable, actual checks and a bounded review policy.

sections.label: Repository contributions
rows: Specifications connected to plans and tasks, with distinct bug and idea processes.
Use the process that fits the task. Inspect specification drift and unnecessary ceremony.
Composable clarification, planning, debugging and review procedures.
Adopt selected procedures. Preserve scope and bound correction/review cycles.
Inspect existing capabilities and make the smallest sufficient implementation.
Check required behavior and maintainability before line count or token claims.
Inspect generated facts and compare task outcomes before adopting them.
Manifests and locked dependencies for sharing agent configuration.
Useful when shared dependency/version management is needed. Installation and permissions remain separate.

sections.label: Procedure
items: Identify the missing procedure and compare doing the task with current instructions.
Read one selected upstream contribution at a recorded revision and identify host assumptions.
Adapt the relevant steps and checks to the current repository. Do not adopt unrelated rules automatically.
Run a small task with explicit acceptance criteria and the configured checks when authorized.
Review requirement completeness, source accuracy, scope, failures and actual effort. Smaller output alone is not success.
Keep or revise the procedure based on observed results. Record limits and an owner for later source drift.

sections.label: Outputs
sections.text: A scoped instruction or procedure, supporting source revision and evidence from the chosen task.

sections.label: Acceptance checks
items: Requested behavior and existing conventions remain intact.
Generated context identifies actual files and commands rather than invented project facts.
Correction loops have a stop condition and do not expand acceptance criteria.
A selected instruction does not supply integrations or runtime permissions.

sections.label: Illustrative example
sections.text: For a status-filter repair, adopt only the diagnosis, scoped-change and regression steps needed for that defect. An unrelated full product design process is unnecessary. Expected output is a small repair packet with observed checks. This example has not been implemented or tested.

basis: Inspected repository documentation and recommended Atlas procedure. Examples are illustrative.
confidence: Moderate for the scoped source contributions. Project fit and workflow outcomes remain unverified.

catalog.applicability: Select useful clarification, planning, implementation and review procedures without importing an entire tool library as policy.
catalog.limits: Reading guidance does not install a repository, select a tool, execute a workflow or establish a passing result. Use actual project versions, commands and evidence.

claims.text: Spec Kit documents distinct specification, bug-fixing and idea-assessment processes.
Ponytail instructs preserving requested behavior and relevant checks while minimizing unnecessary implementation.
